newsitem.title: UK: P&O says also in talks with Brittany Ferries.
newsitem.headline: P&O says also in talks with Brittany Ferries.

text.p: Britain's P&O Ferries, which earlier on Thursday said it planned to merge its Dover-Calais services with those of rival Stena Line, is also seeking cooperation with French-owned Brittany Ferries on the western English Channel, chairman Lord Sterling said.
Sterling told a news conference called to discuss a tie-up with Sweden's Stena Line AB, that talks were underway with privately-owned Brittany Ferries on links on its routes.
P&O corporate affairs director Peter Smith told Reuters there was no timetable for negotiations, however.

Smith explained that Eurotunnel SA/Plc's Channel tunnel service had drawn freight and passenger traffic away from the so-called western corridor of the English Channel where ferries link ports like Poole, Portsmouth and Southampton to Caen, Cherbourg, Le Havre and St Malo in northwestern France.
"Western channel services are losing money, so we do want to do something, but we don't have a specific timescale," he said.

"It makes sense to do something as soon as we can in time for the next season," he added. Most channel routes have a peak passenger season in the summer holiday period and volumes reach their highest levels between May and September.
